non-deterministic.explanation: The server and client rendered different random-looking values (an id, token, or Math.random() output). Anything non-deterministic in render produces a different value on each side.
non-deterministic.suggestion: Use React `useId()` for ids. For random values, generate them after mount (in `useEffect`) or pass a value down from the server so both sides agree. Never call `Math.random()`/`crypto` during render.

date-time.explanation: The values are dates/times that differ between server render and client render — the clock moved (or the timezone differs) between the two environments.
date-time.suggestion: Render the current time after mount, or pass a single server timestamp down and format it identically on both sides. Pin an explicit timezone when formatting.

locale-bidi.explanation: The values differ only by invisible bidirectional control marks (LRM/RLM/isolates). `Intl` adds these around numbers and dates in RTL locales, and different ICU versions — Node vs the browser — emit different ones for the same input.
locale-bidi.suggestion: Format the value in one place and pass the string down, or pin the same locale and timezone on both sides. If the marks are harmless, add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the element.

locale-script.explanation: The same value was formatted with different digit scripts (Arabic-Indic ٠١٢ vs Latin 012). The server and client resolved to different locales.
locale-script.suggestion: Pass an explicit `locale` (and timezone) to `Intl.NumberFormat` / `toLocaleString` on both server and client, or format the value after mount so only the client locale is ever used.

locale-separators.explanation: The same number was formatted with different grouping/decimal separators between server and client (e.g. 1,234.56 vs 1.234,56).
locale-separators.suggestion: Pass an explicit locale to `Intl.NumberFormat`/`toLocaleString` on both sides so the separators match.

locale-date-order.explanation: The same date was rendered in a different field order (MM/DD vs DD/MM) between server and client.
locale-date-order.suggestion: Format dates with an explicit locale and timezone via `Intl` on both sides.

browser-only.explanation: The client rendered content the server left empty — the signature of reading a browser-only API (`window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `navigator`, `matchMedia`) during render.
browser-only.suggestion: Gate browser-only reads behind a mounted flag or `useEffect`, or use `useSyncExternalStore` with a server snapshot so the first client render matches the server.

viewport.explanation: A whole subtree was added, removed, or swapped between server and client — typically a JavaScript width/viewport check that branches the tree at first render.
viewport.suggestion: Render both branches and switch between them with CSS media queries at first paint instead of branching in JavaScript, or defer the JS-driven branch until after mount.

nesting-shape.suggestion:

whitespace.explanation: The mismatch is whitespace-only — the text is identical apart from spaces/newlines. An HTML minifier likely collapsed whitespace around the hydration root differently from React.
whitespace.suggestion: Check your HTML minifier settings (e.g. `conservativeCollapse`) around the app root, or avoid minifying whitespace inside hydrated markup.

third-party-extension.explanation: The attribute `data-gramm` was injected by a browser extension or third-party script (e.g. Grammarly, ColorZilla) before hydration, so the client DOM no longer matches the server.
third-party-extension.suggestion: This is usually harmless. Add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the affected element, or defer third-party script init until after hydration.

third-party-root.explanation: An attribute (`data-foo`) appeared on a root element that the server never sent — a hallmark of an extension or early third-party script mutating the DOM.
third-party-root.suggestion: Add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the root element, or defer the third-party script until after hydration.

third-party-node.explanation: A <iframe> was injected by a third-party script or browser extension (ads, consent, analytics, chat) after the server render. It is not part of your app's hydration, so this is usually harmless noise.
third-party-node.suggestion: If React warns about it, add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the nearest server-rendered wrapper, or load the third-party script after hydration (e.g. Next.js `<Script strategy="afterInteractive">`).

class-added.explanation: The `class` differs between server and client (added on client: wide). A class was applied conditionally on the client — commonly a viewport, media-query, theme, or feature-flag check that runs during the first render.
class-added.suggestion: Render the same className on the server and the first client paint. Move client-only conditions into `useEffect`/a mounted flag, or drive the visual change with CSS media queries instead of a JS class toggle.

class-removed.explanation: The `class` differs between server and client (removed on client: wide). A class was applied conditionally on the client — commonly a viewport, media-query, theme, or feature-flag check that runs during the first render.
class-removed.suggestion: Render the same className on the server and the first client paint. Move client-only conditions into `useEffect`/a mounted flag, or drive the visual change with CSS media queries instead of a JS class toggle.

class-both.explanation: The `class` differs between server and client (added on client: c; removed on client: a). A class was applied conditionally on the client — commonly a viewport, media-query, theme, or feature-flag check that runs during the first render.
class-both.suggestion: Render the same className on the server and the first client paint. Move client-only conditions into `useEffect`/a mounted flag, or drive the visual change with CSS media queries instead of a JS class toggle.

class-neither.explanation: The `class` differs between server and client. A class was applied conditionally on the client — commonly a viewport, media-query, theme, or feature-flag check that runs during the first render.
class-neither.suggestion: Render the same className on the server and the first client paint. Move client-only conditions into `useEffect`/a mounted flag, or drive the visual change with CSS media queries instead of a JS class toggle.

class-arabic.explanation: The `class` differs between server and client (added on client: مخفي, بارز). A class was applied conditionally on the client — commonly a viewport, media-query, theme, or feature-flag check that runs during the first render.
class-arabic.suggestion: Render the same className on the server and the first client paint. Move client-only conditions into `useEffect`/a mounted flag, or drive the visual change with CSS media queries instead of a JS class toggle.

style.explanation: The inline `style` differs between server and client — an inline style was computed from client-only state (viewport size, theme, scroll position) during render.
style.suggestion: Compute the style after mount (`useEffect`) so the first client render matches the server, or move it to a CSS class / media query.

generic-attribute.explanation: The `id` attribute differs between server (`a`) and client (`b`) — its value was derived from something that differs between the server and the first client render.
generic-attribute.suggestion: Make the attribute deterministic across server and client, or set it after mount so the first client render matches the server HTML.

generic-arabic-attribute.explanation: The `title` attribute differs between server (`مرحبا بالعالم!`) and client (`أهلا بالعالم!`) — its value was derived from something that differs between the server and the first client render.
generic-arabic-attribute.suggestion: Make the attribute deterministic across server and client, or set it after mount so the first client render matches the server HTML.

unknown.explanation: A hydration mismatch was detected but could not be matched to a known cause. Inspect the server vs client values above.
unknown.suggestion: Compare the server and client values. Common causes are non-deterministic values, dates/locales, and browser-only APIs used during render.
